# Ad077 — Zero-length aggregates trigger `count-1` underflow / 4 GB loop walk (signed-integer attribute used as unsigned)

**Section**: §12.11 (`12-11-adversarial`)

## Sources
- CVE-2024-23133 (Autodesk ASMDATAX228A.dll on STP)

## Description

A signed integer aggregate-count attribute drives `for(i=0; i<n; i++)` where `n = parsed_count - 1`; if `parsed_count==0`, the unsigned interpretation walks 4 GB before wrap. Common attack shape: multiple zero-length aggregates in one file — `COMPOSITE_CURVE` with empty segment list, `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` with empty knot/multiplicity lists, `ADVANCED_FACE` with empty bounds list, `CLOSED_SHELL` with empty face list — each individually exposes the underflow.

## Reproducer recipe

zero-length aggregate where downstream code expects ≥1.

## Expected kernel behavior

pre-validate count > 0 before computing `count-1`.

Cross-oracle: pure-Python Part-21 validator accepts (`accept`); OCCT crashes (`signal(11)`). The crash is on the kernel side — the file is spec-conformant Part-21.
